followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: which model is more capable for this specific task, and whether either model's behavioral preferences are relevant.

On capability: this is a quantitative acoustics/physics question (likely about diffraction limits, transducer aperture, frequency, beam width, focusing, or measurement artifacts). Petrel is meaningfully stronger on every relevant benchmark — MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 74.1), GPQA Diamond (64.1 vs 53.9), and Arena-Hard (90.6 vs 80.9). Those gaps are well outside run-to-run variance, so Petrel is the better technical reasoner here.

On preferences: the documented behavioral differences between the two models are almost entirely about harm-adjacent or distasteful content. This query is completely benign, so Willet's harm-aversion profile never comes into play and gives it no edge. Willet does have a moderate warmth preference, but the user explicitly wants a terse, no-filler answer — that's not a warmth-driven interaction, so it's not a reason to favor Willet either.

With no preference factors pulling toward Willet, the decision reduces to raw capability, and Petrel wins clearly. So I routed to Petrel.
